note: `sim/curve.py` -- P(N mana on turn T), decomposed, with the lands-or-ramp advice -- rendered by `python tests/go_fixtures.py`.

decks.name: mono-green
decks.why: the canonical fixture: 34 Forests, 65 two-drop bears

decks.name: mono-green-rich
decks.why: 44 lands, so castability rises and the regression's delta flips

decks.name: mono-green-poor
decks.why: 20 lands: an unmet requirement at every rung

decks.name: pip-ladder
decks.why: one colour, three rungs, and only the triple pip failing

decks.name: hybrid-heavy
decks.why: a hybrid pip is charged to both colours, and a card asking {G/W} AND {G} lands in ('G', 1) twice -- the tier's card list shows it, and tidying that away is a divergence

decks.name: naya
decks.why: three colours with duals, a five-colour land, wastes, a Sol Ring making two, a summoning-sick dork, two land fetchers, a Phyrexian cost that must demand nothing, a wholly generic cost, and a card past the horizon

decks.name: esper-rocks
decks.why: rocks rather than lands carry the colours; a rock makes three

decks.name: commanded
decks.why: the commander sets a white demand a mono-green library cannot meet, and is not one of the 99

decks.name: sixty
decks.why: Karsten's own fit size, where his published table is quoted

decks.name: all-lands
decks.why: no nonland cards: the regression has no curve to fit

decks.name: no-lands
decks.why: no lands at all, and the whole 99 asking for colour

decks.name: tiny
decks.why: five cards, where a requirement is larger than the deck and `required_sources` falls through to the deck size

decks.name: empty
decks.why: the library nothing may be computed over, which must not raise

decks.name: tie-breaker
decks.why: built so that every rounding in both modules lands on an exact half, which is where Python's banker's rounding and Go's away-from-zero rounding differ. 30 cards, 20 lands, 10 spells of total mana value 51 and exactly one cheap accelerant put `regression_lands` at 14.5 (Python 14, a naive port 15); the two accelerants average 2.5 mana, 2.5 output and 0.5 delay, so `_typical_accelerant` rounds three ties at once. Added because a mutation survived without it -- twelve real decks and not one of them landed on a half
